title: Arithmetic of Bohr Frequencies Governs Uniform Mixing in Randomly Timed Quantum Spin Chains
abstract: Randomizing the readout time averages the mode interference in a quantum walk. We ask when this makes the site populations of a uniformly coupled $XY$ chain exactly uniform for every initial site. For $N\ge2$ spins, this is possible when $N+1$ is a power of two, a prime, or twice a prime. It is impossible when $15\mid(N+1)$, $21\mid(N+1)$, or $6\mid(N+1)$ with $N\ge11$. Uniformity uniquely fixes the averaged cosine coherences according to the mirror parities of the modes. Equal Bohr frequencies can impose incompatible coherence values. We classify these parity collisions using vanishing sums of roots of unity and prove existence in the positive cases through a phase distribution on a torus.
summary: This theoretical paper characterizes the exact conditions for achieving perfect uniform mixing in quantum spin chains by averaging the quantum walk readout time. It establishes necessary and sufficient conditions based on number theory applied to the system's spectral properties. The work is significant for understanding how spectral arithmetic dictates the long-term, averaged behavior of quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the precise mathematical conditions under which the site populations of a uniformly coupled XY quantum spin chain achieve perfect uniformity after averaging the quantum walk readout time over a given probability distribution.
main_result: Uniform mixing is possible if the number of spins plus one ($N+1$) is a power of two, a prime, or twice a prime, but is impossible if $15$, $21$, or $6$ divide $N+1$ under certain size constraints.
method: The analysis combines spectral graph theory, algebraic number theory (using roots of unity and cyclotomic fields), and convex geometry to analyze the constraints imposed by required coherence values.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the problem of uniform mixing, deriving necessary conditions from the required coherence values, and then using advanced mathematical tools (like phase distribution analysis on a torus) to prove existence in the allowed cases and impossibility in the forbidden cases.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical constraints on quantum transport phenomena, linking spectral properties (Bohr frequencies) to macroscopic physical outcomes (uniform mixing), which is highly relevant to understanding decoherence and thermalization in quantum many-body systems.
